term: hard moral case omission and conflict controls
definition: A Case extends the existing moral-access State with independent Boolean indifference and categorical-reason fields; Reason means the latter is true. The finite controls compare these assignments, then use ideal-successor Ought and feasible Can on two Boolean outcomes. A supplied predicate classifies both outcomes as good. The two ideal frames select opposite outcomes, each feasible in the common available frame.
note: These are analyst stress assignments, not complete theories, source attributions, or claims about metaphysically possible worlds. The outcomes may illustrate promise-keeping versus harm prevention only when an additional interpretation identifies each outcome with the corresponding good; the theorem does not assert those goods or a priority. No implication from non-prohibition to permission is encoded.
